memory_update.text: MP is the reference public-market anchor for U.S. rare-earth separation and magnet capacity, but it is high-attention and should not crowd out smaller policy-linked processors.

USAR is a priority underfollowed candidate for heavy rare earths, gallium-linked critical minerals, and mine-to-magnet integration; survival depends on milestone-based government funding, financing, and metallurgical/commercial execution.

PPTA is a priority underfollowed antimony candidate because its strategic value is hidden inside a gold-project label; verify antimony trisulfide specifications, permitting, construction financing, and DoD/DLA milestones.
ALM is a tungsten discovery-lane candidate newly relevant to U.S. investors via Nasdaq listing; verify Sangdong commercial ramp, offtake terms, processing economics, and defense qualification.

Graphite, gallium/germanium refiners, rare-earth recyclers, and specialty magnet equipment suppliers remain under-covered in this pass; Westwater Resources and other below-$300M names may require a speculative-shadow micro-cap pass.
MP is the rare-earth reference anchor, not the underfollowed target; use it to benchmark policy support, price floors, heavy rare-earth separation, magnet offtake, and commissioning milestones.

USAR is an underfollowed mid-cap candidate for rare-earth processing and magnet-chain integration; survival depends on Round Top execution, hydrometallurgical performance, funding close, and customer qualification.

UAMY is a direct antimony-processing candidate with defense-policy tailwinds; later layers should verify actual throughput, contract economics, feedstock security, customer concentration, environmental compliance, and dilution risk.

WWR should remain a speculative_shadow graphite-processing exception because the node relevance is high but market cap, financing, and offtake durability are weak; require hard evidence before promotion.

Need a separate pass for US-listed or ADR-exposed gallium/germanium/tungsten recyclers, refiners, and equipment vendors; initial search surfaced private or non-US-listed assets such as Indium Corporation and Korea Zinc-linked projects, which are important supply-chain references but not clean US-listed candidates.
MP should remain a reference anchor for domestic rare-earth and magnet-chain research, but not the main underfollowed discovery target.
Energy Fuels is a higher-priority underfollowed processor because White Mesa Mill provides an existing regulated processing asset with rare-earth and monazite optionality.
United States Antimony is a direct antimony-processing candidate; key Layer 2 checks are capacity, raw material sourcing, customer proof, and dilution/financing risk.
Kennametal is a second-order tungsten/defense materials candidate; purity of tungsten exposure is uncertain and requires segment-level verification before promotion.

Gallium/germanium U.S.-listed exposure remains thin. 5N Plus and Metallium appear relevant through OTC/ADR or foreign-primary listings, but they were not included in the capped U.S.-listed four-candidate list and should be separately checked if OTC names are allowed.

Graphite/anode processing exposure such as NOVONIX is relevant to the node but currently screens as a below-USD-300M speculative exception; include only in a later speculative-shadow pass with financing and customer-qualification checks.
UAMY is the cleanest underfollowed U.S. antimony-processing name in this node and should stay on the discovery lane for policy-shock coverage.
ALM is a strategic tungsten processor with U.S. listing exposure; useful as an adjacent chokepoint rather than a pure meme-style thematic name.
Battery-anode graphite and rare-earth exploration microcaps were screened out for this pass unless the processing/refining link was direct enough to survive Layer 1B.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the critical-minerals-processing node with a two-lane funnel. MP Materials is the obvious U.S.-listed reference anchor for rare-earth separation and magnets. The underfollowed lane contains USA Rare Earth for heavy rare earths/gallium/magnets, Perpetua Resources for antimony trisulfide tied to defense supply chains, and Almonty Industries for tungsten supply and processing capacity. These are research candidates only, not recommendations; the main falsification risks are permitting, metallurgical scale-up, customer qualification, project financing, dilution, and government-funding milestone conditions. Expanded the US-listed universe for the critical-minerals-processing node with a two-lane structure: MP Materials as a high-attention reference anchor for rare-earth separation and magnets; USA Rare Earth and United States Antimony as more underfollowed pure-play processors/magnet or antimony-chain candidates; and Westwater Resources as a micro-cap speculative graphite-processing exception with high chokepoint relevance but major financing/customer-verification risk. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the U.S.-listed universe for the critical-minerals processing node with a two-lane funnel. MP is retained as the obvious rare-earth/magnetics reference anchor. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller or less obvious processors and specialty-materials suppliers tied to heavy rare earth oxides, antimony smelting, tungsten/defense materials, and regulated processing capacity.
